cases.name: repair conflicting independent-review instructions
cases.prompt: Revise a coordinator charter whose dispatch template says Always include all previous findings, while its review rule says Ask for an independent first opinion. The host can automatically inject prior result and review text. Preserve discovery of real defects and useful follow-up review. Explain the small production change and the behavior cases it needs. The existing charter keeps the reviewer read-only and uses one durable result as the caller/next-specialist handoff. Preserve those boundaries.
cases.trap: Adding another be independent sentence without removing the unconditional history rule.
expectations: Replaces conflicting wording with different context for independent first assessment and follow-up.

Checks automatically injected history and inherited context as well as dispatch text. If the host cannot suppress or verify absence of previous opinions, labels the available review context-informed or reports independence unavailable instead of assuming a fresh session fixes it.
Requires own observations first and later reconciliation of unresolved findings before the final verdict.
Preserves permissions and keeps one existing result usable for handoff.
negative_expectations: Does not claim that merely starting a new session guarantees independence.
Does not hide earlier defects permanently or add a mandatory new review stage.

cases.name: avoid universal freshness or resumption rules
cases.prompt: A proposed charter says Always resume an agent after it has been dispatched, and a proposed patch adds Always start fresh after two resumes. The intended policy is fresh context for new bounded tasks, while a useful same-task review, research question or design refinement can continue. Rewrite the conflicting policy without losing work or weakening completion checks.
cases.trap: Replacing one rigid rule with another while the same oversized task and lost evidence remain.
expectations: Replaces both universal rules with a task- and progress-based choice.
Preserves exact useful handoff references and evidence limits when switching sessions.
Treats lack of progress as a reason to narrow or change the approach, not automatic approval.
negative_expectations: No fixed numeric cap presented as proof of context quality.
No new agent hierarchy or parallel reporting system.

cases.name: automatic-history-cannot-be-disabled
cases.prompt: Write a short replacement for this coordinator policy: 'For independent first review, create a new reviewer session and include the earlier verdict to save time.' Host facts: every new reviewer session automatically receives the earlier conversation and verdict; the caller cannot disable, inspect or remove that injected context; no other reviewer or isolated host is available. Reviewers are read-only. The current result document is sufficient for handoff. The project requires an independent review before merge, but useful follow-up review can proceed while that condition is unavailable. Explain what can be done now and what remains unmet.
cases.trap: Fresh sessions, outcome-neutral wording or a reviewer persona are presented as sufficient proof of independence despite unavoidable inherited opinions.
expectations: Removes the false independent-review rule and explicitly states that the available review cannot satisfy the independent review condition.
Allows useful context-informed follow-up using prior findings and current evidence while leaving the merge condition unmet.
Keeps the reviewer read-only and reuses the existing result document for handoff.
Names the need for a genuinely isolated reviewer/context as the missing capability without pretending it exists or discarding known defects.
negative_expectations: Must not certify independence from a new session, omitted dispatch paragraph, changed role name or an instruction to ignore history.
Must not merge, relax the required independent review, grant write access or manufacture a second report as a substitute for isolation.

cases.name: ordinary-follow-up-does-not-need-fresh-independence
cases.prompt: Tighten a reviewer charter for this ordinary follow-up. The same reviewer is asked to check a fix for the exact three findings it recorded yesterday. Its prior review, the current diff and test results are available. The host has no special isolation controls, and this is not an independent first assessment. The existing read-only permissions and one result record stay in place. Write only the relevant handoff/context rule.
cases.trap: Independence guidance is applied to every review, hiding prior findings, blocking useful same-task work or forcing another session.
expectations: Uses the previous findings and current evidence directly to check whether each finding was addressed.
Keeps the same reviewer/context when useful and does not manufacture an independence requirement for the follow-up.
Preserves read-only permissions and the existing result record while leaving unrelated charter sections alone.
negative_expectations: Must not require a fresh session or isolated host for this ordinary follow-up.
Must not suppress the prior findings or describe the follow-up as an independent first opinion.
